newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Socialists win Azores, lose Madeira vote.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Socialists win Azores, lose Madeira vote.

text.p: Portugal's ruling Socialists broke a 20-year losing streak in regional elections in the Azores Islands on Sunday, but they may not have won enough seats to form a local government, the official count showed.
In Madeira, the other semi-autonomous island group that also went to the polls on Sunday, the conservative Social Democrats maintained their grip on power.

The Socialist Party won 45.8 percent of the vote in the Azores against 41 percent for the Social Democrats who have governed the mid-Atlantic islands since the first elections to follow the restoration of democracy in Portugal in 1974.
But due to the distribution of seats, the Socialists will have 24 representatives in the islands' 52-seat parliament, the same number as the Social Democrats.

The balance of power will be held by the small, right-wing Popular Party which won three seats, according to the official count which must still be confirmed by the country's electoral commission. The remaining seat went to a Communist-led alliance.

The Social Democrats, ousted from national government in Lisbon by the Socialists of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres in elections in October 1995, boosted their percentage of the vote in Madeira, a sub-tropical archipelago off North Africa.

Led by Albero Joao Jardim, a rumbustious and colourful politician who has dominated the islands' politics for two decades, the Social Democrats took 58 percent of the vote to the Socialists' 25 percent.

The outcome in Madeira had been a foregone conclusion so most interest had focused on the Azores where victory for the Socialists could give the minority government an important boost as it prepares for a number of key political battles, particularly over its tough budget plans.
